Project overview

  • Team: Solo Product Designer & Product Owner, collaborating with 2 Full-Stack Developers and key domain stakeholders.
  • Core skills demonstrated: Product discovery, UML use case modelling, persona architecture, wireframing, usability testing, design systems, data visualisation, FinTech interaction design, agile backlog prioritisation (MoSCoW / Kano).

What this project proves about me: I bridge commercial product strategy and detailed UI/UX execution, turning mathematically dense financial models into friction-free, accessible digital products that users trust.

The challenge

Residential property investment in the UK is heavily skewed toward buying a primary residence, leaving novice investors, accidental landlords, and small-scale developers underserved. When evaluating buy-to-let (BTL) properties, houses in multiple occupation (HMOs), or multi-unit conversions, potential investors face serious hurdles:

  1. Data fragmentation: Evaluating a single deal required cross-referencing multiple disparate calculators (mortgage amortization, gross vs net yield, stamp duty, management fees, void periods, and stress tests).
  2. Analysis paralysis: Inexperienced investors relied on convoluted offline spreadsheets, prone to formula errors and lacking clarity on monthly net cash flow.
  3. High cognitive friction: Existing institutional tools contained intimidating finance terminology and rigid forms that discouraged hypothetical scenario exploration ("What if interest rates rise by 1.5%?").

The business objective was to build an intuitive, web-based property calculator platform that served as a single source of truth for investment feasibility, while driving qualified engagement and advisory leads.

My process

I structured the product lifecycle into five iterative stages:

  1. Discovery & Requirements Architecture: Conducted qualitative user interviews, established domain financial formulas (Gross/Net Yield, Loan-to-Value [LTV], debt-service coverage), and mapped UML (Unified Modelling Language) system interactions.
  2. User Segmentation & Persona Synthesis: Translated qualitative research into three behavioural archetypes to anchor backlog prioritisation.
  3. Information Architecture & Wireframing: Designed user task flows and created low-fidelity responsive desktop wireframes to validate data hierarchy before visual styling.
  4. Prototyping & Usability Testing: Ran moderated "Think-Aloud" sessions on clickable prototypes to evaluate input controls, cognitive load, and visual legibility.
  5. Design System & Delivery Handoff: Refined the UI components into an accessible design system, managed sprint backlogs, and supported frontend implementation.

What I did

1. Requirements Scoping and System Architecture

To ensure technical feasibility and commercial alignment, I led the discovery phase by interviewing property buyers, mortgage brokers, and letting agents. I audited standard financial underwriting equations to guarantee the computational backend produced accurate figures.

I visualised the functional scope through a formal UML use case diagram, mapping primary actors against essential modules: mortgage calculations, rental yield estimators, expense breakdowns, and scenario comparisons.

UML use case diagram detailing system boundaries, core calculation engines, and interaction workflows between user roles and data stores.

2. Persona Architecture

From discovery findings, I synthesised three distinct personas representing varying levels of financial sophistication and differing jobs-to-be-done (JTBD):

  • The Accidental Landlord (Inherited/Relocating): Needs clarity on running costs, tenant management fees, and net monthly cash flow to decide whether to sell or let.
  • The Strategic Property Investor: Needs advanced ROI metrics, stress testing against interest rate shifts, and multi-property comparison capabilities.
  • The Builder / Commercial Converter: Needs rapid calculations on gross development value (GDV), refurbishment cost buffers, and exit yields.

User persona segmentation board synthesising demographic profiles, financial literacy, core objectives, and platform friction points.

3. Information Architecture and Wireframing

To reduce interaction costs during complex calculations, I mapped a two-column desktop workflow: structured inputs on the left, instant live-updating data visualisations and summaries on the right.

I produced low-fidelity structural wireframes to test navigation, content hierarchy, and the arrangement of calculated metrics before committing to visual polish.

Low-fidelity desktop wireframes mapping input forms, mortgage term variables, result card placements, and secondary action layouts.

4. Agile Product Delivery & Value Prioritisation

Acting as Product Owner alongside my design responsibilities, I applied the MoSCoW (Must-have, Should-have, Could-have, Won't-have) and Kano models to manage technical scope within the one-month timeline.

While stakeholders initially requested automated postcode API lookups and complex tax modules for launch, I prioritised a rock-solid calculation engine and side-by-side scenario comparison for the Minimum Viable Product (MVP), pushing live API integrations into Phase 2.

Why I made these decisions

1. Pivoting Away from Gradient-Heavy Aesthetics

  • Hypothesis: A vibrant, high-contrast gradient theme would give the platform a modern, consumer-grade FinTech identity.
  • Observation: During usability testing, users reported visual fatigue when reviewing dense numerical tables against gradient backgrounds. Gradients introduced visual "vibration" and failed Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG 2.1 AA) contrast ratios on small labels.
  • Decision: I eliminated decorative gradients in favour of a restrained palette featuring solid deep blues and high-clarity green accents. This restored legibility, established clear typographic hierarchy, and instilled institutional trust.

Initial V1 mobile explorations using heavy gradient visual styling, later replaced to satisfy accessibility and legibility requirements.

2. Replacing Text Inputs with Reactive Sliders

  • Problem: Manual keyboard entry for variable terms (such as interest rates or property values) caused high friction on mobile screens.
  • Decision: I paired numeric text fields with interactive slider controls. Sliders enabled users to perform rapid, continuous sensitivity testing without repeatedly opening the device keyboard.

3. Iterative Layout Explorations for Data Visualisation

  • Problem: Users struggled to identify whether gross yield or net monthly cash flow represented their actual take-home profit.
  • Decision: I explored four visual card compositions and settled on a prominent "Net Monthly Cash Flow" hero card supported by a circular breakdown chart displaying loan repayments, operational expenses, and profit margin.

Design iterations evaluating visual hierarchy, circular progress metrics, container backgrounds, and contrast treatments for financial outputs.

Images in context

The final product delivered a modular financial application across mobile and desktop breakpoints. The interface separates input variables from real-time dynamic calculations, giving users immediate feedback as terms are adjusted.

Final mobile application screens showing the onboarding value proposition, multi-tool calculator directory, and the dedicated mortgage calculator workflow with reactive sliders.

On desktop and widescreen monitors, the platform leverages a structured dashboard grid. Users can evaluate side-by-side scenarios simultaneously, comparing purchase price variations against net rental returns without losing input context.

Final responsive desktop web application views demonstrating side-by-side comparison tables, clean white-space management, and accessible data visualisations.

Impact / results

Area Result Context / Validation
Investor Confidence +40% increase Measured via post-launch user surveys comparing task confidence against traditional spreadsheet calculations.
Engineering Velocity +20% faster build Reusable component library and documented token states reduced development turnaround compared to internal benchmarks.
Calculation Sessions High repeat engagement Users consistently ran multiple calculations per session, validating the reactive slider "What-If" interaction model.
Accessibility Compliance WCAG 2.1 AA Solid colour token architecture and revised typography solved visual fatigue identified in early testing.

Strategic Product Metrics Framework

To measure ongoing product performance beyond the initial release, I defined tracking criteria:

  • North Star Metric: Calculation Sessions per Active User (validating regular utility during property acquisition cycles).
  • Conversion Rate (CvR): Percentage of completed calculations resulting in a saved PDF report or mortgage advisor referral inquiry.
  • Task Completion Time: Time-to-first-result reduction tracked across input slider interactions.

Strategic Roadmap: Phase 2

  1. Live Market Data API: Integration with property portals (Zoopla / Rightmove) to automatically fetch area average rents and historical capital appreciation by postcode.
  2. Regulatory & Tax Engine: Dedicated calculation modules for Stamp Duty Land Tax (SDLT) surcharges and Section 24 mortgage interest relief restrictions.
  3. Portfolio Dashboard: Multi-property tracking allowing landlords to monitor cumulative portfolio yield and upcoming refinancing dates.

Tools and skills applied

Category Tools / Skills
UX Research & Strategy User Interviews, UML Use Case Diagrams, Persona Development, JTBD, MoSCoW Prioritisation, Kano Model
UI & Interaction Design Figma, Interactive Prototyping, Wireframing, Responsive Design, Design Systems, WCAG 2.1 AA
Testing & Analytics Think-Aloud Usability Testing, Metric Frameworks (CvR, Task Completion, Retention)
Product Delivery Backlog Grooming, Sprint Planning, Jira, Developer Component Handoff

Roles performed on this project

  • Lead Product Designer: Information architecture, wireframing, design system creation, prototyping, usability testing, and WCAG accessibility compliance.
  • Product Owner: Requirements definition, user research, UML system mapping, backlog prioritisation (MoSCoW), stakeholder alignment, and developer handoff.

Entry-level property investors and accidental landlords often struggle with fragmented financial calculators and dense spreadsheets, leading to analysis paralysis or costly investment mistakes. As the solo Product Designer and Product Owner, I led the end-to-end initiative to design and architect a centralised, conversion-focused property investment calculator.

Grounding the product in user research, I conducted qualitative interviews, mapped UML use cases, built targeted personas, and ran iterative wireframing and usability testing. When initial testing revealed that high-contrast gradient visual styling hindered data comprehension, I pivoted to an accessible, modular design system with responsive layouts across mobile and desktop.

The final solution delivered an intuitive multi-tool investment engine featuring live yield calculations, interactive what-if sliders, and side-by-side scenario benchmarking. Post-launch user validation demonstrated a 40% increase in investor confidence compared to traditional spreadsheets, while the modular component library accelerated frontend engineering delivery by 20%.
